account:
Today I have kept my appointments, though correspondence and the survey handover took longer than expected. No council letters were available. The secretary mistakenly handed me the appointment book, which I returned; she has now delivered the builder's actual survey. I paid his agreed two-emerald fee. His report records successful passage over the bridge and on the ferry, with no specific defects observed, but expressly excludes concealed structure and nighttime lighting tests. It is not a safety certification, and I have authorized no repairs.

The unusual matter remains talk of changes to the bridge or port without any identifiable plan. Earlier the innkeeper denied proposing such changes and traced only a vague rumour to Townsfolk 03. Builder has no verified proposal details. Today Freight likewise reports hearing mention of changes but knows no details or official notice. His warehouse is empty, and he approached me at cottage tea asking whether municipal cargo transport was needed. That could simply be his search for work; I have no evidence of another purpose or secret arrangement. He says the ferry is available on the east bank.

The neighbour is here for our scheduled tea, but has not yet supplied news. The secretary has been handling records and confirms my office appointment at half past four. The baker was advertising stocked bread earlier; I heard later distant speech but could not understand it, so cannot connect it to these rumours. My concern is that discussion is circulating without reaching me, but I cannot yet tell whether there is a real proposal behind it or merely repeated speculation. I should trace concrete sources and distinguish witnessed facts from hearsay rather than accuse anyone.
